Create one new illustration for an illustrated book of modern fairy tales, showing the moment described below.

Picture: Midstream in the great river on a cold, grey day. Rich Per has just come up out of the icy water, coughing and furious, his expensive long overcoat spreading out around him and turning black. The Ferryman stands in the current beside him and looks at him with a face like stone. On the near bank behind them, two big lorries, three trailers and a huge cool bag wait by the water's edge.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Rich Per: A tall, bony businessman of about sixty with a long, horsey face, a jutting chin, a sharp hooked nose, small, darting, greedy grey eyes, a thin mouth, long bushy salt-and-pepper sideburns and slicked-back black hair streaked with grey, with a sharp widow's peak. He wears an expensive long wine-red wool overcoat over a charcoal suit, a green-and-gold striped silk tie, polished black shoes, a heavy gold signet ring and a chunky gold watch.
- the Ferryman: A small, wiry, very old man, bent almost double with a back as crooked as a fish hook, yet strong as an ox. He has a wrinkled nut-brown face, a sharp beak of a nose, bright little black eyes under bushy snow-white eyebrows, a toothless grin, no beard, and thin white hair tied at the back in a stubby pigtail. He wears a battered straw hat, a faded sea-green anorak with patched elbows and grey work trousers rolled up above the knee, and goes barefoot.

Story world: Present-day Norway, in a long inland valley where Rich Per owns half of everything. Just below his big modern house, an old stone mill house stands by a fast river; a couple of dozen kilometres downstream is a second old mill with a wooden waterwheel under the floor. The chest is a small, polished oak box with a heavy brass lock, its seams sealed with tar. Per's letter is a sealed white envelope. The thieves' hideout is a shabby smallholding deep in a spruce forest, and the young couple's smallholding lies up under a bare ridge. Far away runs a great, wide river with no bridge, and above it a fortress-like house of grey concrete and dark glass is built into the mountain. The three feathers are long, shining golden feathers.

This story's season, light and colours: A raw, grey November: low cloud and fog along the rivers, wet asphalt and gravel, black spruce, the last yellow birch leaves plastered to the ground, and dusk by four in the afternoon with orange street lights and warm lit windows. In the concrete house: cold blue-white light, black glass and the glint of gold.

Art style: Contemporary Scandinavian editorial illustration: flat, graphic shapes with subtle risograph grain and a little hand-drawn texture, clean confident lines and a limited palette of spot inks led by deep petrol blue, with fjord teal, lingonberry red, honey mustard, sage green, warm paper off-white and ink charcoal, like the pages of a risograph-printed book, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, in the cool, clear Nordic light of today. Present-day Norway: fjord towns, suburbs, farms with tractors, cabins, ferries, roadside petrol stations, offices and flats, grey rain and bright snow, with people in modern clothes such as rain jackets, knitted sweaters, hoodies, suits and work wear. The magic of the tale appears plainly in this everyday world: trolls, talking animals and enchantments look real and slightly absurd, drawn in the same flat style. Every character has their own face, build, age, hair and clothes exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Dry humour, careful composition with one focal point and plenty of negative space. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles, logos, signs or readable screens. Phones and screens show only light or simple shapes.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Suitable for readers of all ages: no blood, wounds or gore, and no killing shown. Show danger and cruelty through atmosphere, posture and suspense, never through injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.
